A one-month-old female infant is brought to her pediatrician for a routine wellness check. Her feeding
pattern includes 6-7 daily breastfeeding sessions lasting 30 minutes each, with 8-10 daily urinations
and 4-5 loose, yellow "seedy" stools. She sleeps 10 hours at night and takes 3-4 naps of 2-3 hours
each. Her mother notes that compared to her siblings, this infant cries more frequently, typically for
20-30 minute periods up to 4 times daily, usually before feeding and more intensely in early evening.
While swaddling and rocking provide limited comfort, an infant swing seems most effective in calming
her. Growth charts show height and weight at the 60th and 70th percentiles respectively. Vital signs
include temperature 98.0°F (36.3°C), blood pressure 81/58 mmHg, pulse 134/min, and respiratory rate
28/min. Physical examination reveals a comfortable infant with a soft, flat anterior fontanelle, normal
eye and ear examinations, and a soft, non-tender, non-distended abdomen. She demonstrates midline
tracking ability. What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Milk protein allergy (B)
Attachment disorder (C) Infantile colic (D) Early autism spectrum disorder (E) Feeding intolerance (F)
Sensory processing disorder (G) Infant regulatory disorder (H) Sleep-wake cycle disturbance (I)
Gastroesophageal reflux disease (J) Normal infant crying
 A. Feeding intolerance
B. Early autism spectrum disorder
C. Attachment disorder
D. Normal infant crying
